title: Mass on a spring

reference.basis: no object of known size is visible; animation scale is arbitrary

slow_motion.evidence: no narration, caption or on-screen text indicates slow motion

subjects.description: small orange rectangular block attached to the bottom of the vertical spring

observation.what_happens: An orange block hanging from a vertical spring moves up and down in front of a grid. The oscillation continues freely throughout the clip with no visible release or stop.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The s channel shows ~0.3 s period vertical oscillation around ~50 pixels with peaks falling from ~97 to ~70 and troughs rising, indicating weak damping. x is flat noise, path is straight, so 1D motion along s is sufficient. Candidates go from ideal to linear-damped to linear plus quadratic air drag to nonlinear stiffness to test damping and amplitude dependence on the held-back data.

critique.finding: The block wiggles around a rest spot at {s_eq} with a natural rate of {omega0}. Each swing shrinks steadily because of gentle friction set by {gamma}.
critique.headline: Spring block hums evenly while gentle friction steals motion
critique.why_it_won: It nails the slow shrinking of the swings while extra air drag or spring stiffness add nothing useful.

headline: Spring block hums evenly while gentle friction steals motion
finding: The block wiggles around a rest spot at 50.8 ± 0.018 pixel with a natural rate of 20 ± 0.0015 1/s. Each swing shrinks steadily because of gentle friction set by 1 ± 0.003 1/s.

eyeball.confidence: low - only three near-static frames visible, estimates are order-of-magnitude guesses
eyeball.law_in_words: Vertical damped harmonic oscillator: acceleration = -omega0^2 times displacement from equilibrium position s_eq minus gamma times velocity.
